You're getting a lot of different answers here. My understanding (which may be incorrect) is that this started shortly after WWI.

Back then, Liberalism meant things like free inquiry, free thought, treating people as equally under the law, and so on. It became associated with science, and with the objective, open pursuit of truth.

Leftism around this time was warming to the idea of a scientifically-run society - what we would later call a technocracy. Using the modern methods of organization and management, good government could be efficiently provided to all. These leftists - who mostly called themselves Progressives - embraced liberal positions while they rallied for changes to the traditional social institutions defended by those who wanted to conserve them; folks we would later call conservatives.

The left did not hijack Liberalism itself, but they eventually did manage to steal the name, because they loudly advocated Liberal views as a tactical means of advancing their Progressive goals. The easiest example of this is to note that 1960s-era Berkley was both a center for progressive thought, and a center for free speech advocacy. The left needed the freedom of speech to advance their progressive goals.

Decades pass and the left now owns most of the cultural institutions - the colleges, the press, Hollywood, the public schools. Now free speech is no longer a tactical advantage for them, and indeed, it is now just mostly threat which might be used against them by their opponents. Suddenly we have hate speech laws and PC language police and safe spaces. But the word 'Liberal' remains associated with the Left, as an irony and as an obscure historical artifact.
